newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares ended up on active buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares ended up on active buying.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed up 2.83 percent on Monday on active buying, with sentiment improving after the market's robust performance last week, brokers said.
The B share index gained 4.21 points to end at 153.27 points on volume of 32.17 million shares worth HK$165.37 million compared with Friday's HK$90.82 million.

The market's steady rises last week triggered follow-up demand on Monday, one broker said, adding that a strong rise in market heavyweight Changan Automobile coupled with heavy trade boosted investor confidence.
Changan soared HK$0.27 to HK$4.80 on the day's most active trade of 4.21 million shares.
"The market is being supported by optimism over China's overall economy this year and I expect share prices to rise slowly over the medium term," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
"Trading could turn volatile in coming sessions as it is the last week before the two-week Chinese new year holiday," a broker said.
Dadonghai Tourism, the sharpest gainer, jumped HK$0.35 or 9.21 percent to HK$4.15 on trade of 3.32 million shares on institutional buying, brokers said.

Beverage maker Shenbao put on HK$0.42 or 7.37 percent to HK$6.12 after 510,841 shares changed hands. Guangdong Expressway climbed HK$0.53 or 6.98 percent to HK$8.12, but volume was relatively thin at 284,700 shares.
Building materials producer Fangda, the biggest loser, dropped HK$0.07 to HK$8.78 on trade of 690,450 shares due to profit-taking, brokers said.
The A share market maintained upward momentum on selective buying in shares of firms likely to announce good results and attractive dividends for 1996, brokers said.
The A share index edged up 6.13 points or 1.68 percent to finish at 370.81 points on turnover of 7.37 billion yuan against the previous session's 7.05 billion yuan.
Hengyang Chinese Medicine closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 8.43 yuan, with 3.58 million shares traded.
